messages:
maya: Heads up — bringing up aurora-13b-quant-v1 on dedicated. Quick smoke shows odd tokens in the middle of responses and a measurable quality drop vs HF baseline. I dumped the tokenizer+added_tokens and there looks like an ID shift for special tokens (bos/eos/pad/unk). @samir can you eyeball?

samir: Can you paste the converter inspect output and the small added_tokens snippet?

maya: Pasting the two small excerpts. first, converter inspect: 
```
$ hf_to_redwood inspect-tokenmap aurora-13b 
special tokens (hf_id -> rw_id):
  bos_token: 1 -> 1295
  eos_token: 2 -> 1296
  pad_token: 0 -> 0
  unk_token: 3 -> 1297
added_tokens (hf file): ["<|bos|>", "<|eos|>"]  # no explicit ids in hf added_tokens.json
```
And the small section of the tokenizer files we shipped: 
```json
// added_tokens.json (hf)
{
  "added_tokens": [
    "<|bos|>",
    "<|eos|>"
  ]
}
// tokenizer.json (redwood-converter output snippet)
{
  "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<|bos|>", "eos_token": "<|eos|>"},
  "vocab_size": 50280
}
```

maya: The main point: hf didn't give explicit ids for these added tokens, converter appends them at the end which made their rw_ids large (1295 etc). Then the quantizer seems to repack indices and we get different id allocation at runtime — responses contain the literal string tokens or the wrong token id is interpreted as an ordinary token, producing sequences like: "Hello <|bos|> there" or truncated outputs.

kevin-b: I've seen this pattern. When added_tokens.json has no "id" field, HF tooling often appends at end and different versions of the tokenizer/merge scripts pick different insertion points. The quant pipeline (vocab repack for int8 kernels) can reorder token ids to optimize layout, which breaks any assumption that special token ids are stable.

samir: How bad is the eval regression? numbers?

maya: Ran our instruction-following eval (5k prompts) quickly:
- hf baseline (float): pass@1 ~ 86.1
- redwood quantized variant (current onboarding): pass@1 ~ 79.3
- harmlessness score down ~4 pts on our safety subset
Also saw qualitative failures where the model emits a BOS token mid-generation. Sample: 
```
input: "Summarize this document"
output (bad): "Summary: The study shows... <|bos|> moreover, the key points are..."
```

kevin-b: Two short-term fixes: 
1) During conversion, preserve explicit ids for added tokens. If HF added_tokens lacks ids, inject them using the original HF vocab offsets (best-effort) with `--force-add-token-ids`.
2) Add runtime fallback: map special token strings back to expected semantic ids before decoding. This means if decoder sees an unknown id that matches a known string, treat it as BOS/EOS. Ugly but buys time.

maya: I put up a tiny PR with (1) a conversion flag and (2) a test that replays the HF tokenizer -> converter -> quant pipeline and asserts special token strings are still recognized. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/convert/pulls/2378 (draft).

deploy-bot: build #2378/5 failed — unit test `token-map-preserve` failed on macos-latest.

maya: failing test reproduces the issue: quant repack step still changes token ids for the mac build. Looking into quant tool options.

kevin-b: We should also consider canonicalizing special tokens into tokenizer metadata (i.e., include explicit "id" in added_tokens.json during model onboarding). For future model onboards require the HF tarball to include a pinned tokenizer.json that lists ids. I'll put a checklist item in the onboarding template.

samir: For rollback plan: do we have a safe fallback to unquantized or to older token mapping?

maya: Yes — I've scheduled a rollback of aurora-13b-quant variant from dedicated pool and re-enabled float variant for traffic. Rolling back now.

infra-bot: rollback started for cluster: prod-dedicated-gpu-2. Estimated time ~3m.

maya: Follow-ups: (a) add converter option `--inject-added-token-ids` (b) extend our ingestion CI to run small token-id-stability check (run hf tokenizer, converter, quantizer, compare token->string mapping for special tokens), (c) update onboarding checklist to require explicit added_tokens ids in HF packages. I'll add items to the PR and to the onboarding doc.

samir: thanks — once PR is green we should re-run the full eval to confirm fix. :eyes:

kevin-b: note for docs: also call out SPM vs byte-level behavior — sentencepiece may encode explicit special tokens differently. Add a short note in the converter README.

maya: filing a short incident note in postmortems/ — saving eval diffs and samples. Will ping when PR passes.
